$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the contract shape the prompt asks for, JSON only with no prose
and no fence, and it is the baseline every other fragment-selection case is measured against. It is
also the only case where every required fragment is chosen and no forbidden one is, so both metrics
sit at their best value and any matching change moves them.

A frozen copy of one real eval case. The pair (expect, stdout) is the whole input to scoreCase, so
the expect block is stored here rather than read from evals.json: a replay has to keep scoring the
scenario it was derived against even after the live eval data moves on, and
`npm run test:eval-data` already guards the live data against the step files.

the whole line and parses, and the seven names come back unchanged because none carries a knowledge/
prefix. selection is those seven names in the order the reply gave them.
scoreCase compares that set against the frozen expect block. mustLoad has 7 entries and the chosen set
contains all 7, so missing is empty and hits is 7 - 0 = 7. mustNotLoad has 3 entries and the chosen set
